correctness.rationale: Valley after k-th down step has (k,u), kb≤u≤nb−1, realized by U^u D^k U^(nb−u) D^(n−k); summing allowed u yields b*n(n−1)/2 vertices. For n≥3, the only isolated vertex is (1,nb−1). An explicit admissible word joins every k≥2 vertex to (1,b); every nonterminal (1,u) joins (2,nb−1), and that joins (1,b). At n=2 all b vertices are isolated. At n=3 the graph is bipartite with A_u=(1,u),B_v=(2,v) and precisely u<v edges. Counting gives 3b vertices, E=b(3b−1)/2, components sizes 1 and 3b−1, and first Betti E−(3b−1)+1=(3b−4)(b−1)/2; no higher-dimensional faces. The isolated singleton has degree 1 in nonpure grading; evaluating Mu–Welker f(x,y−1) yields both stated h coefficients. All universal quantifiers follow from admissible-word constructions, not small enumerations.
residual_risks: Length-three graph homotopy does not imply complete higher-dimensional topology at n>3; the claimed unrestricted part is only the component count.
Small b edge cases b=1 are included with beta_b=0 and two connected components.
